output.summary: A flowering plant native to eastern and central North America. Usually living for two years, it forms a low leaf rosette first, then sends up a flowering stem whose yellow blooms open quickly each evening and last until the following noon. Most parts are edible: roots and leaves may be raw or cooked, while young stems should be peeled before eating raw or fried.
output.edibilityNote: Indigenous North Americans historically used it as food; roots and leaves are eaten raw or cooked, while young stems are peeled before eating raw or fried.
